## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One policy defect needs fixing: the new `--exclude` flag does not read its default from an `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` environment variable, which project policy requires for every new flag under `cli/`. This review found no other defects in the exclusion logic or its tests.

## Changes
The pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag. `collect` uses it to skip files whose basename matches any of the patterns and logs each skipped path. The pull request also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md`, adds unit and end-to-end tests, and adds a one-line text fixture.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Default --exclude from ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE env var — A CI job that sets `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` gets no exclusions, because `--exclude` uses `default=[]` and never reads the environment. Policy at `.claude/skills/cli-flags/reference.md:5` says: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI pipelines that set options through the environment cannot use the new flag. — Fix: Set the default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` (for example, split on a documented separator), add the variable to `docs/flags.md:7`, and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` to cover the environment value.
